title: Scripture and the Gospel
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture and the Gospel teaches that the Bible reveals humanity’s sin and God’s saving answer in Jesus Christ. The Gospel is not separate from Scripture; it is promised, prepared, fulfilled, proclaimed, and guarded through God’s Word.
summary: Scripture and the Gospel teaches that the Bible reveals humanity’s sin and God’s saving answer in Jesus Christ. The Gospel is not separate from Scripture; it is promised, prepared, fulfilled, proclaimed, and guarded through God’s Word.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the good news revealed in Scripture. His death, burial, resurrection, and saving reign fulfill God’s promises and provide the only way for sinners to be reconciled to God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Bible reveals the Gospel from promise to fulfillment. Scripture begins with God as Creator, exposes the ruin of sin, announces God’s promises, prepares the way through covenant and prophecy, and reveals salvation accomplished in Christ.

The Gospel is according to the Scriptures. Christ died for sins, was buried, and rose again on the third day in fulfillment of God’s Word. The apostles did not invent a new message disconnected from the Bible; they proclaimed what God had promised and fulfilled.

Scripture also guards the Gospel from distortion. It shows that salvation is by grace, through faith, in Christ, not by human merit or another message. Any gospel that removes sin, weakens the cross, denies the resurrection, or replaces Christ with human achievement is false.

The Bible is therefore not merely a book of religious advice. It is the written revelation of God’s saving work, calling sinners to repent, believe, and find life in Jesus Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without Scripture, people may redefine the Gospel into self-help, moral improvement, religious performance, social approval, or vague spirituality. They may use Christian words while losing the message that actually saves.

This doctrine keeps the church centered on Christ crucified and risen. The broken need more than encouragement. The guilty need more than advice. The lost need more than inspiration. They need the Gospel God has revealed in His Word.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let Scripture define the Gospel for you. Do not assume every message that mentions Jesus is faithful to the biblical Gospel; test what is taught by Scripture, especially what it says about sin, grace, the cross, the resurrection, repentance, faith, and the lordship of Christ. Learn the biblical message, believe it personally, guard it carefully, and proclaim it clearly.
